## Description

A large oval ciliate (~250 µm; 173–335 µm depending on the population) with trichocysts, which
swallows whole diatoms, flagellates and pieces of algae; it is often seen full of brown and green
vacuoles. It also eats desmids.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 2 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A raptorial feeder with helical swimming. Its `mouth_width` (~70 µm, half the body width) lets it
swallow a *Cosmarium* (~66 µm) but not a *Staurastrum*, whose arms make it wider: the
[defence of processes](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md#mouth-width). Width ~55 % of the length
(estimated).

## Literature

- Foissner W. (description) and Serra V. et al. (2021) BMC Zool. 6: 4 (173–335 µm by population).

## Unique and shared mechanics

Its mouth width is the clearest example of the [process defence](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md);
shares helical swimming and conjugation with the other ciliates.
